placements.note: The review places the experimental building 'between Halls A and B', not in one hall; the Atlas hall sites of LNGS share one campus-grade point, and Hall A is used as the nearest named hall. The placement is therefore approximate by construction.
placements.quote: the experimental building of the experiment was built between Halls A and B in Gran Sasso

active_mass.quote: The total active mass of the detectors is 10.96 kg

enrichment.quote: The Ge crystals were grown out of 19.2 kg of 86% enriched 76 Ge material.

isotope.quote: The Ge crystals were grown out of 19.2 kg of 86% enriched 76 Ge material.

summary.plain: Five germanium crystals, enriched in germanium-76, cooled in a lead and plastic shield deep under the Gran Sasso mountain; each crystal is at once the source of the decay and the detector that records it.
summary.technical: Five p-type HPGe crystals (19.2 kg of 86 % enriched 76Ge in total, 10.96 kg active mass); four in a common 30 cm lead shield in a radon-free nitrogen atmosphere with 10 cm borated polyethylene and scintillator veto, one in a separate copper and lead box.

technology.quote: The Heidelberg–Moscow experiment operates five p–type HPGe detectors in the Gran Sasso Underground Laboratory.
technology.value: Five p-type high-purity germanium detectors made from germanium enriched in 76Ge, in lead and borated-polyethylene shielding under nitrogen, with pulse-shape analysis
